description: Eight-way switch that plays its inputs in an order you type in, giving each one a length in clocks, with a crossfade at the changeover and a trigger when each turn begins

params.text: Sets how many clocks this row plays for before the order moves on, 1 to 64
Starts counting clocks on the first press and writes that count into this row's length knob on the second; the lamp on it is lit while it is counting
Sets how many clocks before the changeover the crossfade starts, 0 to 16; at 0 the crossfade starts at the changeover itself
Sets how long the crossfade takes, 0ms to 1000ms; at 0 the switch is instant

inputs.text: Each rising edge above 1V counts one clock towards the length of the input now playing, and towards any length being learned
A rising edge above 1V returns to the start of the typed order and cancels any learning in progress
The signal that is passed to the output while this row's turn comes round

outputs.text: Whatever the row now playing is being fed, crossfaded with the row before it while a fade is running
A one-millisecond trigger at 10V at the moment this row's turn begins

notes: type the order into the black strip below the clock jacks: digits 1 to 8 in any arrangement, spaces and commas allowed, and a hyphen for a range, so 1-4 stands for 1, 2, 3, 4.
an empty strip plays all eight rows in turn.
nothing moves on until a clock reaches CLK. The output carries whatever the first row in the order is being fed until then.
the crossfade only happens where the next row is a different one; a row named twice over carries straight on.

inputs.0:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
